about.title: Susanville Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Lassen County's public records show 14 injury collisions and 18 injured people in the most recent year, with reports clustering on Tuesday afternoons between 2 and 4 p.m. — a pattern that often lines up with school and work traffic converging along Main Street, Paul Bunyan Road, Skyline Road, and Rt 36. Whatever road you were on, the days after a crash matter. Insurance adjusters move fast, sometimes asking for a recorded statement before you've even seen a doctor. We handle car accident claims directly — we evaluate what happened, help preserve evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, or witness accounts before they disappear, and speak with the insurance company on your behalf. There's no fee unless we recover compensation for you, and reaching out costs you nothing.
about.ctaText: Get your free case review today — no obligation.

items.title: California's Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like Lassen County or Caltrans — was involved. Talking to us early helps make sure that deadline never becomes the reason a claim gets denied.

items.title: Comparative Fault Means Partial Blame Doesn't Erase Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for the crash, you can still recover a reduced amount tied to the other driver's share of fault. We can help make sure your side of the story — and the fault percentages — are represented accurately.

items.title: No Cap, No Upfront Cost
items.desc: California doesn't limit non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases, and we work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless we recover money for you. That structure lets you focus on recovery instead of legal bills.

items.question: Should I give the insurance company a recorded statement after a crash on Rt 36 or Main Street?
items.answer: It's best to avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer before speaking with us. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim later. We can handle those conversations for you.

items.question: What if my crash happened on a county-maintained road near Susanville?
items.answer: If a Lassen County road or Caltrans-maintained route like Rt 36 was involved, special notice requirements and shorter deadlines — sometimes as little as six months — can apply when a government entity may share fault. It's important to get legal guidance quickly so you don't lose that option. Contact us to discuss these timelines.

items.question: Do you charge anything to review my case?
items.answer: No. We provide a free case review — there's no charge for us to evaluate your claim. If we take your case, we typically work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if we recover compensation for you.
